analysis:
Examined the protocol-messages.md excerpt, the GLM fixture README, the libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule bump, and EngineV2Bridge+Submission.swift (patch plus base text).

The bridge change adds a pre-admission refusal (head ~lines 153-157 and ~964-994). A native-tracked engine now rejects token-constrained requests and logprob requests the engine cannot capture, with a typed unsupportedOutputControl error. This runs after the shutdown guard and before duplicate-ID tracking, service allowance, KV reservation and cache staging. The refusal path calls usageSignal?.finalizeLookup(.policy) and continuation.finish(), then throws. No reservation, receipt, staging or ready-receipt registration has happened yet, so I see no leak of resources or prefix-cache state (T-041). The nonthrowing overload maps the error to an in-band error marker, which is a fail-closed behavior. Security impact is positive: it avoids untyped 500s that could trip the coordinator's inference-error breaker (availability), and it adds no plaintext exposure or auth change.

Unverified points: (1) whether the error marker string, i.e. EngineV2Translation.unsupportedOutputControlPrefix, is mapped to a 400 downstream; (2) the README now says strict tools, forced tool choice and JSON modes are served by validating generated output before exposure. Enforcement lives in code not supplied, and the README explicitly says the fixtures do not qualify those modes. This is a documentation claim whose validation implementation (the output-validation path) should be checked by integration. It is not a regression shown here. (3) The libs/mlx-swift-lm submodule moves from 7bed821 to baca4ac with no diff visible, so its contents are unreviewed. It sits in the inference engine boundary (TB-007) and executes with decrypted prompts, so the supply-chain change warrants review of the submodule diff. The protocol docs excerpt is documentation-only, with reasoning-control semantic changes, and shows no security-control change.
